Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
The worst possible single operation corresponds to a vertex whose out-degree is maximized, which in a simple directed graph with |V| vertices is at most |V| - 1. Using aggregate analysis, the total cost of all |V| operations is the sum of the out-degrees of every vertex, which equals |E|, so the average amortized cost per operation is |E| / |V|.

* The worst-case cost of any single operation in the sequence is |V| - 1, which is realized when a particular vertex v has a directed edge to every other vertex in V, giving it the maximum possible out-degree.
* The average amortized cost, computed as (total cost of the sequence) / (number of operations) = |E| / |V|, follows directly from the observation that the sum of the out-degrees over all vertices in a directed graph equals the total number of edges |E|.
